pages.title: From image to inspectable candidate fits
pages.subtitle: Local browser interface → Python analysis → evidence, candidate labels and reproducible exports.
pages.sources: Source: web/app.js · server.py · engine.py · workbench_project.py · folder_paths.py

nodes.title: 1  Select an image and analysis settings
body: Browser controls the image/ROI, enabled phases, detector settings, reference cells and display. Requests carry an explicit settings snapshot.

nodes.title: 2  Local HTTP service
body: server.py validates requests, serializes engine access and manages grid jobs, saved entries and exports.

nodes.title: 3  Validate and load calibrated pixels
body: Engine loads finite 2D DM4 or bundled demo arrays. Calibration units choose real-space FFT or direct diffraction.

nodes.title: 4  Extract observed profiles  →  panel 2
body: FFT: crop, window, transform and detect peaks.
Diffraction: detect spots in recorded pixels; optionally refine one shared beam centre.

nodes.title: 5  Compare periodic structures  →  panels 3–5
body: Generate allowed HCP/BCC/FCC predictions; fit rotation/scale, assign peaks, score and screen.
A separate freely fitted reciprocal-grid check reports one or two periodic patterns.

nodes.title: 6  Return numerical results and display fields
body: Profiles, candidate models, rank components, geometry, flags, settings, timings and engine hash.
Browser renders overlays, tables, previews and exports.

nodes.title: Image collection
body: data/ and output/ point to chosen locations; .tem-paths.json records the choices.
DM4 metadata supplies calibration. Bundled NPZ/JSON demos include pixel checksums.

nodes.title: Material and structure inputs
body: materials.py: editable nominal cells and phase defaults.
templates.json + crystal_templates.py: a finite set of zone axes and reflection rules.

nodes.title: Display is separate from fitting
body: Palette, contrast, marker shape/motion and Raw FFT / Processed view do not rerun fitting.
Processed view exposes the smoothed background-subtracted signal; the original FFT remains available.

nodes.title: Many ROIs  →  panel 6
body: A background grid job calls the same analysis for each cell. Adaptive refinement decides which children replace a parent.
Current implementation: sequential cell analysis. SciPy FFT uses two workers; grid parallelization is not implemented.

nodes.title: Keep and reproduce
body: Browser storage: basic preferences.
Project: named ROIs, source identities, tags and settings. Exports: numerical JSON and separate PNG/GIF visuals.

nodes.title: Interpretation
body: Candidate labels are not confirmed phases.

pages.title: Two routes to measured reciprocal-space profiles
pages.subtitle: Coordinates are in nm⁻¹ (cycles per nm, without a 2π factor). Detection uses calibrated source pixels.
pages.sources: Source: analysis_core.spectrum · diffraction.spectrum · diffraction.py centre and spot helpers

nodes.title: REAL SPACE  /  ROI → FFT
body: z = (I − mean(I)) × W; mean removal and Hann W are optional.
L = log(1 + |fftshift(FFT₂(z))|²). Frequency bins follow the crop: Δg = max[1/(w·sx), 1/(h·sy)]. Display spans ±1.05·gmax.

nodes.title: DIRECT DIFFRACTION  /  detector → coordinates
body: No FFT: qx = (x − cx)·sx; qy = (cy − y)·sy.
Initial centre: clusters of opposite-spot midpoints, with a central prior and beam-stop shadow cue; detector midpoint is the labelled fallback.

nodes.title: Remove radial background and smooth
body: Bin radius by floor(|q|/Δg); subtract the mean L in each radial bin.
D = Gaussianσ(L − radial_mean). Default σ = 0.65 FFT bins. The Raw FFT / Processed toggle shows L or D with the same coordinates.

nodes.title: Find spots across position and size
body: Masked Gaussian differences at σ and 2σ; check successive scales (2, 4, 8, 16, 32 detector pixels by default).
Find spatial/scale maxima; compare filtered response AND native intensity against local annular background.

nodes.title: Threshold connected profiles
body: Within gmin ≤ |q| ≤ gmax: T = max(Tfloor, f·max(D)).
Default Tfloor = 1.8; f = 0.35. One maximum per connected component of D > T; require maximum ≥ minimum strength.
Auto strength searches subsets of this pool (panel 4). It does not lower T or change σ.

nodes.title: Local contrast, centroid and deduplication
body: Background annulus: 4σ–8σ. Strong spots must exceed the user contrast cutoff in both response and intensity (default 9).
Positive-core centroids and spot widths refine positions. Strongest-first suppression merges nearby detections of the same spot across scales.

nodes.title: Refine positions and keep independent evidence
body: Parabolic x/y refinement, limited to ±0.5 bin. Fold q and −q to one profile; strongest-first merge below the larger of the user separation and window width.
Default cap: 70 profiles. Weight w = clip(Dpeak − 2, 1, 6).

nodes.title: Optional shared translation refinement
body: At least 3 opposite pairs spanning directions: robust least squares fits their common midpoint, within the shift limit (default 50 px).
Redetect once if the centre changes. Reject inconsistent/competing origins; HCP, BCC and FCC share the same centre.

nodes.title: FFT matching tolerance
body: Approximate window power width: 1.44·Δg (Hann), 0.886·Δg (rectangular crop).
Matching radius τ = max(0.10 nm⁻¹, window width). Default fitting band is 3–10 nm⁻¹, adjustable. Full outer-band Nyquist coverage is required for phase fitting.

nodes.title: Direct-spot profiles and tolerance
body: Group observed opposite spots once; never invent a missing partner. Weight w = clip(log(1 + contrast), 1, 6); default cap 70.
τ = max(0.10 nm⁻¹, estimated spot width). Default band: 2.5–10 nm⁻¹; centre/masks exclude obscured areas. Only observed spots are marked.

pages.title: Generate, rotate and scale allowed patterns
pages.subtitle: Predictions move to match observations. Image pixels, reciprocal axes and measured peak coordinates do not stretch.

nodes.title: 1  Reference unit cells
body: Material presets supply editable a₀ and c₀. Cubic: a = b = c. HCP: a = b, γ = 120°.
Only enabled phases enter the search. Zone directions form a finite library; this is not an exhaustive orientation search.

nodes.title: 2  Enumerate integer reflections
body: Cubic: g(hkl) = (h, k, l) / a.
HCP: g(hkl) = ((2h+k)/(√3·a), k/a, l/c). Internal indices use three coordinates.
BCC: h+k+l even. FCC: h,k,l all even or all odd. HCP: exclude odd l when (h−k) is divisible by 3.
Keep zone-law hu+kv+lw = 0; project onto its reciprocal plane.

nodes.title: 3  Supply enough reciprocal nodes
body: Integer bounds depend on reference dimensions, outer radius and smallest allowed scale; no fixed shell count.
Each scored prediction is filtered again to the current radial band. q and −q represent one profile.

nodes.title: Allowed does not mean visible
body: These rules generate positions, not simulated intensities. Thickness, excitation, contrast transfer and masking can hide reflections.
No multislice, dynamical-intensity, ring-indexing or stacking-fault model is used.

nodes.title: 4  Apply a physically defined metric
body: Cubic / uniform: one multiplier. HCP dual modes: sa and sc where c is visible. Each remains within 0.85–1.15.
For plane basis P and D = diag(sa,sa,sc), use metric M = PᵀD²P and transform √M. Model a = a₀/sa; c = c₀/sc.
New overall + c/a coordinates: s = √(sa·sc); r = (c/a)/(c₀/a₀) = sa/sc. No extra tight ratio cap.

nodes.title: 5  Seed orientations and scales
body: Use up to 16 strongest observed profiles to seed in-plane rotation and reciprocal scales.
HCP dual search scans 11 c*/a* ratios plus 1, then continuous refinement. Fast nearest-neighbour quality must reach 0.20.
Retain up to 4 dual-scale or 3 single-scale seeds per template.

nodes.title: 6  Alternate assignment and refinement
body: Assign peaks one-to-one (right), then solve weighted positional least squares for rotation and visible scales.
Up to 3 rounds; rotation moves at most ±0.06 rad per round. Accept a new solution only if its position score does not decrease.
Scale penalties are applied after this positional optimization.

nodes.title: 7  Retain distinct fits
body: Rank by the adjusted score (panel 4). Keep up to 5 per phase; suppress near-identical profile assignments within the same zone in automatic mode.

nodes.title: One-to-one profile assignment
body: For observed oi and predicted pj:
dij = min(||oi − pj||, ||oi + pj||)
Qij = exp[−½(dij/(τ/2))²] if dij ≤ τ; otherwise Qij = 0.
The same tolerance is used for every structure.

nodes.title: Hungarian assignment
body: Minimize costs −wi·Qij, with zero-cost dummy columns for unmatched observations.
A measured profile can support only one node within a candidate; a prediction cannot claim several profiles.
Matched opposite spots count once.

nodes.title: Fixed-scale path
body: Stored/custom scale uses fixed dimensions. Seed rotations at 0.5° increments; refine rotation twice, capped at 2° per step.
The best 2 quick seeds per template are evaluated. Fixed-mode retention suppresses duplicate support within a phase, even across equivalent zones.
No automatic scale cost applies.

nodes.title: Search limits
body: Finite zone library and seed budget: “best” means best retained candidate found by this search, not a guaranteed global crystallographic solution.

pages.title: Build the rank, screen the fit, select peak strength
pages.subtitle: All scores are heuristics. Peak coverage is weighted detected-profile coverage, not an intensity fraction or phase probability.

nodes.title: 1  Positional evidence minus chance agreement
body: Let W = Σi wi and M be the one-to-one matched pairs. Coverage C = Σ(i,j)∈M wi / W.
Position score P = Σ(i,j)∈M wi·Qij / W − Σi wi·ci / W.
ci = min(1, Σj 1[||oi|−|pj|| < τ] · (2/π)·asin(min(τ/max(|oi|,0.1),1))).
RMS = √mean(dij²) over matched pairs, without intensity weighting. Chance correction accounts for prediction density.

nodes.title: 2  Scale preference
body: Existing modes: S = λ mean[((sₖ − 1)/0.05)²]. Fixed mode: S = 0.
Overall + c/a: S = λ[ln(s)/ln(1.05)]² + μ[ln(r)/ln(1.05)]²; s = √(sa·sc), r = sa/sc.
λ = μ = 0.10 initially. No ratio cost if c is invisible. Ranking preferences, not strain limits or parameter-count corrections.

nodes.title: 3  Check additional weak maxima and unsupported predictions
body: Search unmatched prediction sites within r = max(0.10, window/spot width). Exclude strong-peak neighbourhoods; use one-to-one weak assignments. In FFT mode this separate weak detector uses σ = 0.65 bins, a 1.8 floor and local annular median/MAD contrast.
For assessable sites, weak qualities include distance and bounded local contrast. B = max(0, weak quality per predicted node − mean of 11 rotated-control values).
F = unsupported predictions / assessable predictions. Edge, masked or unreliable sites are unchecked rather than penalized. Missing predictions are not proof of absent reflections.

nodes.title: 4  Adjusted rank
body: R = P − S + η·B − η·F. λ controls overall scale; μ controls c/a in ratio mode; η controls peak evidence. Default λ = 0.10 and η = 0.10.

nodes.title: 5  Acceptance screen
body: Require ≥4 original strong matched profiles, directional spread max|sin(θi−θj)| > 0.5, C > 0.30, P > 0.20 and final R > 0.20.
Weak maxima change rank but do not count toward four strong profiles. Passing is compatibility evidence, not a confirmed phase.

nodes.title: AUTO STRENGTH  /  reuse one FFT
body: Build the strongest-first component pool with minimum strength set to zero. Other thresholds, smoothing, separation and profile cap remain active.
Each distinct component strength defines a possible retained peak set.

nodes.title: Fit every admissible distinct set
body: Sweep the admitted strengths, including cutoffs stricter than the manual value. Recompute matching and weak-site evidence for each set.
Do not stop at the first passing fit. If ≥4 profiles exist, do not explore subsets with fewer than four.

nodes.title: Select the best passing rank
body: Prefer sets with a passing candidate; among them maximize R. If none passes, keep the highest-ranked rejected result.
Equal ranks retain more profiles. Report selected strength, number of sets and trial scores.

nodes.title: Apply per ROI or per grid cell
body: The chosen set supplies the displayed profiles, classification and saved result. Selecting a threshold cannot manufacture an independent confirmation.

nodes.title: Cached reweighting
body: Changing λ, μ or η can rerank stored candidates without repeating the FFT. It keeps the chosen profile set; rerun Auto analysis/grid to re-optimize the strength.

pages.title: Interpret competing fits and periodic geometry
pages.subtitle: Passing candidates can describe the same evidence or separate evidence. Those cases produce different labels.

nodes.title: No phase assignment
body: Fewer than 4 detected profiles → Insufficient evidence. Otherwise → Phase unresolved.

nodes.title: Choose the highest-ranked passing fit
body: Its matched profile IDs form the primary evidence set. Search other passing candidates for independent evidence beyond this set.

nodes.title: Separate-evidence result
body: Require ≥3 new strong profiles, nonparallel spread >0.5 and >15% of total profile weight. Different phase → Two candidates; same phase → Multiple orientations.

nodes.title: Shared-evidence result
body: Rank gap <0.08 and >60% of primary IDs shared with another phase → Ambiguous. No separate population is established.

nodes.title: Otherwise: compatibility or unresolved
body: Primary weighted coverage >45% → compatible with that structure. Otherwise → Phase unresolved. The independent-evidence test takes precedence over near-tie ambiguity.

nodes.title: Additional shared-evidence ambiguity check
body: If a compatible leader and another passing phase match exactly the same profiles, but the leader uses more scale parameters or more unsupported prediction positions, retain Ambiguous.

nodes.title: PARALLEL CHECK  /  geometry only
body: Seed two reciprocal basis vectors from the 16 strongest profiles. Round observations to integer coefficients and fit the basis by weighted least squares (up to 3 rounds).
Search is bounded by basis length, area, angular spread and coefficients −4…4. No crystal structure is assigned.

nodes.title: Primary reciprocal grid
body: Require ≥4 matched profiles, nonparallel spread ≥0.5 and at least one coupled basis coefficient.
Geometry score = position-weighted coverage − chance allowance − 0.03. Primary passes with score >0.25 and coverage ≥50%.

nodes.title: Secondary reciprocal grid
body: A second grid must pass score >0.20 and coverage ≥30%, with ≥3 new strong profiles in nonparallel directions.
Rejected or duplicate support is not exposed as a detected secondary geometry. Identical primary evidence does not establish another pattern.

nodes.title: Dominance and downstream use
body: Dominance = primary coverage / (primary coverage + unique secondary weight fraction). A valid secondary is substantial when dominance <80%.
Geometry supplies an independent explanation and can trigger adaptive refinement. It does not choose the HCP/BCC/FCC phase winner.
Candidate-labelled image area is not a measured phase fraction.

pages.title: Adaptive regions, cached fits and saved state
pages.subtitle: Every accepted grid cell runs the same numerical pipeline. Refinement changes the map partition, not the detector physics.
pages.sources: Source: server.py grid jobs · adaptive_refinement.py · engine.rescore · workbench_project.py · web/app.js

nodes.title: 1  Create a breadth-first region queue
body: Start with an n×n uniform grid (2–24 per side). Analyse each region using the submitted settings; maintain the currently accepted map leaves.

nodes.title: Keep current leaf
body: No split if adaptive is off, a child is <32 px, or its physical width would fall below the chosen stopping limit.

nodes.title: 2  Split uncertain or multiple-pattern regions
body: Unresolved, insufficient, ambiguous, two-candidate or multiple-orientation results request subdivision. A substantial geometry-only second pattern also requests subdivision.
Queue four children when size limits allow.

nodes.title: 3  Optional “Check passing regions”
body: Even a passing parent can test four children. Keep them if a child supports a new phase/zone, a separate pattern, or if the children mix passing and unassigned results.
A new phase/zone must beat the parent family on that same child by ≥0.08 rank, or the parent family must be absent/below screen.

nodes.title: 4  Commit a subdivision or retain the parent
body: All four merely lose evidence → retain the parent. Same interpretation without a split trigger → retain the parent. Accepted subdivisions replace the parent and can refine recursively.
Passing-parent trial children do not count as map leaves until accepted. Cancelled/incomplete trials leave that parent intact.
Map totals use current leaf areas; subdivided parents and rejected probes are excluded.

nodes.title: Reweight an existing map
body: Compressed candidate pools retain explored fits, including rejected fits. Changing overall/axis penalty λ, c/a penalty μ or peak weight η recomputes ranks, labels, symbols and totals without another FFT.
Cell boundaries and selected detected profiles stay fixed. Reweighting is not a fresh scale/rotation/strength search; rerun the grid when those choices need optimizing again.

nodes.title: Basic preferences and linked folders
body: Browser localStorage remembers basic analysis/display settings and per-image diffraction choices. Folder links are stored separately in .tem-paths.json.
Preferences are not a backup of the source data or a saved analysis.

nodes.title: Reusable named regions
body: tem_workbench.project.json stores image identity, ROI coordinates, settings, name, tags and notes. Writes use a revision check and atomic replacement.
Reopening recomputes the analysis. The project does not embed an FFT bitmap. Hover previews are a cache, not the scientific record. Original images stay in their linked data locations.

nodes.title: Exports and provenance
body: Numerical result/grid exports preserve settings, observations, fit evidence, classifications, source pixel checksum and engine hash. PNG/GIF exports separately capture the rendered view.
The browser draws the same axes and overlays for original FFT and processed detector signal. Diagnostic exports identify the Processed view; changing display never changes the numerical fit.
This atlas is versioned alongside the source. A hash check flags relevant code changes for diagram review; regeneration does not infer algorithm changes automatically.
